study: Hoefer, Lindner, Ayasse & Kuppler (2022), Sinapis arvensis rainfall manipulation
study_design: 53 source plants distributed over five rain shelters, three original rainfall treatments, mother-family IDs, different treatment plots; 427 visitor-group source rows not 427 plants
source_grain: same plantID must agree on motherID, treatment, shelter and plotID across all three measured tables
source_visitor_exposure: observetime is repeated per visitor-group row; sum NrInteraction but use observetime only once per plant
primary_endpoint: original estimated seedsperplant, transformed log1p for squared-error forecast, NOT offspring establishment
heldout_unit: whole original rain shelter, five folds; original plant only once in each heldout yearless fold

frozen_models.M0: precipitation treatment and log1p(total seasonal flower count)
frozen_models.M1: M0 plus mean floral display size and mean petal width
frozen_models.M2: M1 plus log1p(sum visits divided by unique plant observation time in hours)
frozen_models.M3: M0 plus identical visitation predictor for secondary direct diagnostic

visitation_identity_placebo.unit: within original shelter by rainfall treatment label, shuffle plant visitation predictor one-to-one
visitation_identity_placebo.qualification: exploratory descriptive within-archive identity control, NOT a causal randomized p-value

strict_process_readiness: M2 vs M1 positive average equal-shelter gain, positive individual-weighted gain, positive gains at least four/five shelters, and exceeds site-treatment visitor-identity shuffle q97.5
limitations: The original paper already observed rainfall effects and relative roles of flower supply and visitation; not a new discovery.
No individual genomic sequence: motherID is an ancestry-family label, not a molecular genotype measurement.
No longitudinal descendant flower traits or functional ancestral pigment molecular pathways.
Observed visits over time and total seasonal flower counts share period with seed output, not sequential experimental mediation or true prospective deployment.
Rainfall treatments are assigned in original shelters/plots and original insect taxa are not automatically effective pollinators.
Five shelters from one published study are NOT independent studies or evolutionary radiations.
No numeric transfer of Cirsium bagging or Ipomopsis corolla-width effect sizes.
registration_note: retrospective source-audited analysis designed after prior SDEA and original published results; not prospective or preregistered biological effect
